Do not include undead, skeletons, wraiths, Open Vale, the Custodian, or the Hanging Office. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.

Long Storyboard: This roll teaches Daggerheart and sets an early ethical tone. A compassionate party may earn a future warning. A violent party may alert the true ambushers. Run this scene as threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test: The first meaningful roll teaches that this adventure is about judgment, not just success. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.
Read Aloud: The strixwolf lowers her head. Her feathers rise along her spine. The pups go still. What do you do?

Gm Notes: Track Strixwolf Mercy. Good treatment can pay off as warning before the Bramble Union ambush. Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it. Manufactured-threat lens: seed the contradiction, do not explain it. The surface goal stays simple and heroic.
Sensory Details: leaves shaking after the mother retreats the crate answering with one low pulse a corporate route bell too cheerful for the scene
Body Language: Varian's bow lowers slowly Marlowe makes herself stop staring at the blood
Sample Dialogue: Marlowe Fairwind Good. We kept the job intact and did not make the world smaller.

Checks: Any relevant approach Resolve fallout from the creature encounter. Easy to hard by choice Record trust, blood debt, or neutral outcome. 20 Cleanly resolve: Resolve fallout from the creature encounter. Add a concrete boon, extra clue, or improved position. Success, plus the player names one helpful detail or asks one follow-up question. Success, but the GM exposes a cost, ticks a countdown, or reveals a new pressure tied to The First Roll. The full goal slips, but the party still learns a useful truth or avoids the worst consequence. The GM makes a hard move that follows from the fiction and leaves the next choice visible. Spend Fear to reveal omitted risk, split attention, or put a human cost in front of the contract. On mixed or sliding results, reveal information in layers: visible fact, actionable clue, then systemic truth.
Choices Consequences: Pause to reassess The party earns a cleaner investigation beat. Lower Act Two surprise risk. Push forward The job stays on schedule. The ambush feels sharper.
Clues: Feather token A sign of danger. GM can use it to foreshadow the ambush. Only appears if mercy was shown.

Player Questions: What detail in The First Roll tells you the official story is incomplete? Who notices the human cost first, and how do they show it? What small object, smell, or sound makes this scene feel real?
Relationship Prompts: Which PC quietly checks on someone else here? Who disagrees about the right thing to do without breaking trust?
Ownership Prompt: Name one detail in The First Roll that belongs to your character's point of view.

Reveal Hooks: Loreborne or Knowledge-focused PCs can read the institutional layer. Wildborne/community-focused PCs can read local custom and ecological stress. Martial/security-focused PCs can read threat posture and custody logic. Magic-focused PCs can feel ward tone, soul-signal, or spell instability. Loreborne: spots older legal, heraldic, or ward-craft language under the branding. Underborne: notices service doors, hidden routes, and who built the thing nobody credits. Highborne: reads etiquette, class panic, and reputational risk. Ridgeborne: notices stonework, weight, pressure, and structural weakness. Wildborne: reads the land, animals, and local ecological stress. Elf/Ribbet/Human/Giant/Katari: invite one sensory or social detail from the player's heritage. Sorcerer/Rogue/Warrior/Guardian/Ranger: give each class one table-facing way to shine without changing the plot.

Fear Spends: Spend Fear to reveal omitted risk, split attention, or put a human cost in front of the contract. Make the safe road feel less safe: noise, scent, cracked wheel, or cargo hum. Separate evidence from assumption so a monster read is tempting but incomplete.

Story Scope: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end. Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy. The Strixwolf Mother is feeding pups and guarding them; she reacts to tone, not bloodlust. REFLAVOR GUARANTEED Presence to calm; Instinct to read boundaries The driver died from a cut throat; the strixwolf did not kill him. KEEP EARNED Instinct or Knowledge Medium 15 Near the cart is a pre-written Grail "Hazard Confirmed: Strixwolf Attack" tag. ADD EARNED Finesse or Instinct Medium 15 Helping the pups or sparing the mother earns Hope now and can create a later warning boon. ADD SEED Presence: calm the mother. Instinct: read the scene. Knowledge: notice behavior mismatch. Finesse: search the cart.
